oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Management of traumatic tarsal septic bursitis in a Brahman cow with long-term intravenous regional limb perfusion
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Shelby-Hobbs, Loren D.
Smith, Joe S.
Hecht, Silke
Mulon, Pierre-Yves

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: A 3-month-pregnant 5-year-old Brahman cow was presented with a 4-day-old tarsal wound and left hind lameness. A diag­nosis of traumatic septic tarsal bursitis was established. The wound was debrided and cleaned, revealing exudate pock­ets and bone exposure. The cow underwent multiple proce­dures, including debridement of the calcaneus, and received ongoing treatment with antibiotics, pain management, and wound care. Despite initial progress, the wound developed complications, including progressive osteomyelitis and soft tissue swelling. Lameness in the affected limb fluctuated from moderate to non-weight-bearing (grade 4/5 lameness). Treat­ment consisted of bandage changes and regional limb perfu­sions performed under sedation. To preserve venous access, a long-term catheter was placed in the lateral saphenous vein. Improvement was seen after each surgical debridement, but recovery was slow, and the prognosis remained guarded due to damage to the calcaneus/calcaneal tuberosity and superfi­cial digital flexor tendon involvement. Additionally, care was taken to avoid medications that potentially affect gestation. After several weeks of treatment, the wound showed signs of healing with granulation tissue and eschar formation. By day 48, the cow was discharged with instructions for continued care, antibiotics and lameness monitoring. During her treat­ment, she maintained her pregnancy and calved 6 months fol­lowing discharge.
